name: LM334MX_NOPB
title: LM134/LM234/LM334: 3-terminal adjustable current sources, 1 µA to 10 mA
summary: A floating, three-lead current source whose current, 1 µA to 10 mA, is set by one resistor from R to V− and holds from 1 V to 40 V across the part with 0.02%/V regulation. The setting voltage is 64 mV at 25 °C and proportional to absolute temperature, so the part doubles as a two-wire temperature sensor; LM234-3 and LM234-6 are specified for that use at ±3 °C and ±6 °C. Initial accuracy is ±3% (LM134/LM234). LM134H/NOPB is the LM134 (−55 °C to +125 °C) in the hermetic TO metal can.
key_figures: 1 V to 40 V (30 V for LM234-3/-6)
3% max LM134/LM234, 6% max LM334, 10 µA to 1 mA, V+ = 2.5 V

notes: LM334M and LM334MX take the SOIC-8 pinout; LM334SM and LM334SMX the alternative SOIC-8 pinout.
MX and SMX parts come on 2500-piece reels; M and SM in 95-piece tubes.

circuits.title: Basic current source
circuits.description: The simplest connection: one resistor from R to V- sets the current. The current entering V+ is the sum of the resistor current and the chip's own bias current, both leaving at V-.

circuits.title: Zero tempco current source
circuits.description: R1 carries a current that rises with temperature, set by VR across it. R2 sits across both VR and a forward-biased 1N457, whose falling forward voltage makes its current drop with temperature. With R2 about ten times R1 the two slopes cancel and ISET hardly moves with temperature; the example values give 1 mA.
notes: R1 and R2 values are the 1 mA example of the design equations.

circuits.title: Ground referred Fahrenheit thermometer
circuits.description: The LM134 runs with its V- at ground and a 100 Ω resistor from R to ground. A PNP stage carries the current up through R1 so that VOUT reads 10 mV/°F from 10 °F to 250 °F. A 2.5 V reference feeds the R node through R3, which is trimmed to calibrate; R3 = VREF/583 µA.

parts.note: feeds the reference from +VIN; no value given
reference; any stable positive voltage of 2 V or more serves as VREF

notes: VOUT = 10 mV/°F for 10 °F ≤ T ≤ 250 °F; +VIN ≥ 3 V.

circuits.title: Terminating remote sensor for voltage output
circuits.description: The sensor and its RSET sit at the far end of a pair of wires; the load resistor RL at the receiving end turns the current into a voltage. With RSET = 230 Ω and RL = 10 kΩ the output is 10 mV/K. Wire resistance in series does not change the current.
notes: VOUT = ISET × RL; the line between V- and RL is the long run to the sensor.

circuits.title: Low output impedance thermometer
circuits.description: The output is taken at the R pin, where the current through R1 and R2 gives 10 mV/K. The R pin looks like a negative resistance of about −R2/16; the 600 Ω series resistor R3, equal to R2/16, cancels most of it so that ZOUT stays at or below 100 Ω. C1 stands across R2. The supply must be at least 4.8 V.
notes: VOUT = 10 mV/K, ZOUT ≤ 100 Ω, VIN ≥ 4.8 V.

circuits.title: Low output impedance thermometer with transistor
circuits.description: A PNP transistor driven by the LM134's V+ current supplies the load from its collector at the R pin, bringing the output impedance down to 2 Ω or less at 10 mV/K.
notes: VOUT = 10 mV/K, ZOUT ≤ 2 Ω.

circuits.title: Higher output current
circuits.description: A 2N2905 PNP carries most of the current: the LM134's V+ current drives its base, and its collector feeds RSET at the R node. R1 and C1 in series from base to collector are chosen for best stability.

circuits.title: Basic 2-terminal current source
circuits.description: The two-wire current source: RSET from R to V-, the current entering at +VIN and leaving at -VIN. This is the connection the set-current error figures refer to.

circuits.title: Micropower bias
circuits.description: The LM134 with a 68 kΩ RSET draws 1 µA from the programming pin of an LM4250 programmable op amp. The LM134's V- and RSET return to the amplifier's negative supply.
notes: The bias current drawn from the LM4250 is 1 µA. INA and INB are the amplifier's two inputs.

circuits.title: Low input voltage reference driver
circuits.description: A reference diode D1 (LM129, LM136, LM113 or similar) sits between the output and the R node, with R2 = 120 Ω from R to ground; the LM134 then holds 64 mV across R2, so VOUT is VZ plus 64 mV at 25 °C. A 2N4250 PNP whose base current runs through the LM134 supplies up to 3 mA at the output, and the input need only be 200 mV above VREF.
notes: VOUT = VZ + 64 mV at 25 °C, IOUT ≤ 3 mA, +VIN ≥ VREF + 200 mV.

circuits.title: Ramp generator
circuits.description: The LM134 charges C1 with a constant current, so VOUT ramps up linearly; a pulse on RESET turns on the 2N2222 and discharges C1, giving a sawtooth.

circuits.title: 1.2 V reference operating on 10 µA and 2 V
circuits.description: A 1.2 V reference built from the LM134 alone: R2 across R and V-, and R1 in series with a 1N457 from V- to ground. The ratio of R1 to R2 is chosen for zero temperature drift. The output is taken from R through R3 and may supply up to 1 µA.

parts.note: 1%; ratio to R2 chosen for zero drift
1%; ratio to R1 chosen for zero drift

notes: VOUT = 1.2 V, IOUT ≤ 1 µA, +VIN ≥ 2 V.

circuits.title: 1.2 V regulator with 1.8 V minimum input
circuits.description: A 2N4250 PNP pass transistor, its base current drawn through the LM134, regulates a 1.2 V output. Between the output and the common line are a 1N457, R1 and R2, with the R pin at the R1-R2 junction; the ratio of R1 to R2 is chosen for zero drift. Output current is up to 200 µA.

parts.note: 1%; ratio to R2 chosen for zero drift
1%; ratio to R1 chosen for zero drift

notes: VOUT = 1.2 V, IOUT ≤ 200 µA, VIN ≥ 1.8 V.

circuits.title: Zener biasing
circuits.description: The LM134 feeds a zener with the current RSET sets; VOUT is taken at the zener.

circuits.title: Alternate trimming technique
circuits.description: A variable resistor R1 between V- and the output end trims the current. For a ±10% range, RSET is chosen 10% high and R1 is about three times RSET.

parts.note: variable resistor, wiper tied to one end

circuits.title: Buffer for photoconductive cell
circuits.description: A photoconductive cell takes the place of RSET, so the current through a meter in series with the LM134 and a 1.5 V cell follows the light level.

circuits.title: FET cascoding for low capacitance and/or ultra high output impedance (FET at V+)
circuits.description: An N-channel JFET in series at the V+ end, its gate tied to the -VIN end, lowers the capacitance across the source and raises its output impedance. The FET must leave at least 1 V across the LM134.

circuits.title: FET cascoding for low capacitance and/or ultra high output impedance (FET at V-)
circuits.description: The same cascode with the JFET at the V- end: its gate goes to +VIN, its drain to the LM134's V- and RSET, and its source to -VIN.

circuits.title: Generating negative output impedance
circuits.description: R1 from +VIN to the R node makes the two-terminal impedance negative, about −16 × R1. R1/VIN must stay below ISET.

circuits.title: In-line current limiter
circuits.description: The LM134 sits in the positive supply line of an op amp and limits its current to the value RSET sets. C1 on the protected supply is the smallest value that keeps the protected device stable, which keeps the inrush into a short low.

parts.note: minimum value for stability of the protected device

operation.text: The part is a floating current source with three leads and no separate supply pin. One resistor from R to V− sets the current anywhere from 1 µA to 10 mA, a 10,000:1 span, with 1 V to 40 V across the part. The sense voltage that sets the current is 64 mV at 25 °C and is proportional to absolute temperature, so the plain one-resistor source has a tempco of about +0.33%/°C. Adding a diode and one more resistor gives zero drift.
Reversed by up to 20 V, the part passes only some tens of microamps, so in AC use it acts both as a rectifier and as a current source.

LM134 is rated from −55 °C to +125 °C, LM234 from −25 °C to +100 °C and LM334 from 0 °C to +70 °C. LM234-3 and LM234-6 are specified as temperature sensors with an initial accuracy of ±3 °C and ±6 °C. Packages are the hermetic TO can, TO-92 and SOIC-8.

Because the output is a current proportional to kelvin temperature, series resistance in long wires costs no accuracy, and only two wires are needed. Most of the initial error is a slope (gain) error rather than an offset, and the output extrapolates to zero at 0 K whatever RSET is. A single gain trim at one temperature therefore corrects slope and zero together; either RSET or the load resistor can take the trim. Slope error after trim is normally under ±1%.

RSET sits at about the part's temperature, so its own drift adds straight to the slope: 33 ppm/°C costs 1%. Metal film parts below 20 ppm/°C serve, and wire wound parts give the best stability. A remote RSET takes three wires and suffers lead resistance, and is not normally recommended.

Above a threshold rate of change of voltage the current can shift non-linearly. The threshold scales with ISET: 0.01 V/µs at 10 µA and 1 V/µs at 1 mA. Faster slewing does not damage the part or cause large currents.

Above 100 µA self-heating, not the electrical regulation, sets how ISET moves with voltage. At 1 mA the junction warms about 0.4 °C in still air per added volt across the part; at 0.33%/°C that is a 0.132% current change, ten times the electrical figure. A heat sink on the TO can, or on the TO-92 leads, reduces the effect more than threefold.

The part has 15 pF across it, which limits AC output impedance and may load the circuit. A FET in cascode with the part brings this under 3 pF and improves regulation by at least ten times; DC behaviour is unchanged apart from a higher minimum voltage.

Current noise is about four times a transistor's shot noise. Used as the active load of a transistor amplifier it raises input-referred noise by about 12 dB, and a single stage can reach a voltage gain over 2000.

The sense voltage is under 100 mV, so thermocouple and lead resistance effects matter: RSET goes physically close to the part and sockets are best avoided. At 1 mA, 0.7 Ω of contact resistance lowers the current by 1%.

The sense voltage rises about +0.23 mV/°C while a silicon diode's forward voltage falls about −2.5 mV/°C. In the zero tempco circuit I1 and I2 each carry about half of ISET. The 1N457 is the diode named for it, its tempco centred at 11 times that of the LM134, which allows R2 = 10 R1. For the lowest drift with a given diode and current the circuit is built and measured over temperature: R2 is reduced if the tempco is positive and increased if negative. Setting the tempco equation to a non-zero target gives a source with a chosen tempco. The diode tempco is best measured or taken from its maker.
ESD protection is limited: leads are kept shorted together or the part kept in conductive foam during storage and handling.
